title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 4,000 deaths
summary:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo, a country in central Africa, is facing a very large Ebola outbreak. Ebola is a serious disease caused by a virus. Congo announced the outbreak on May 15. The health ministry said on Thursday that 4,018 people have died. That is nearly half of the 8,300 confirmed cases. It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. The virus is a rare type called Bundibugyo, and there is no known treatment or vaccine for it.

Fighting the outbreak is hard. In the city of Bunia, some health workers gathered to ask for wages they are owed. Officials quickly sent them away. Some of them do surveillance work, which means finding people who were near a sick patient. Front-line workers have gone on strike several times since the outbreak began.

Safety is another problem. A senior United Nations official said soldiers burned a camp that included a transit centre for Ebola patients while they were searching for weapons. About 19,000 people in the camp had to leave. Julien Harneis, the UN senior Ebola co-ordinator, said that when a centre is lost, its capacity and investment are lost too, and the work has to start again. More than 50 health workers have died after catching the virus.

There are some signs of change. Confirmed cases have slowed, from around 850 cases a week in mid-July to an average of 490 a week in September. But Africa CDC said this could be because of insecurity and trouble getting communities to co-operate. In some places the spread has slowed, and in others it has sped up.
why_it_matters: Ebola outbreaks affect whole communities. Unpaid workers, strikes and unsafe areas can slow the work of finding and helping sick people, so health care needs steady money, staff and safety.
